monsterFluff.name: The Pleurossa Fungus & the Mushroom Dragon

entries: {@style {@font The mushroom dragon is the corrupt creature born from the pleurossa.|Zethandriel}|large}

entries.name: Consumption and Control
entries: Once, a party of adventurers—Amina the bard, Kaltaar the druid, Izora the sorcerer, and Zethandriel the barbarian—set out to research floral dragons and share what they learned with the world. After traveling together for a while, they split up to better investigate dragons in different habitats. The adventurers planned to reunite in the village of Peskarii, home to Izora, to share what they had learned about floral dragons.

However, while the adventurers wandered the world, they remained unaware of a floral dragon close to home. A haughty and short-tempered {@creature Wisteria Dragon|FGoFD24} that laired in the deep forest turned its cruel gaze toward the village of Peskarii. It demanded tribute and servitude from the villagers.

When they were unable to meet the dragon's extortionate demands, the wisteria dragon choked the settlement's land with its grasping vines. The people of Peskarii fell into an enchanted slumber and starved to death.

When Izora and her party returned to Peskarii, their excitement to share their findings was erased by the sight before them. The bones of Izora's friends and family lay entwined in wisteria flowers throughout the ruin of her village. Filled with grief and a venomous hatred for the dragon that destroyed her home, Izora swore revenge. Her friends warned her that the dragon was too dangerous to take on and urged her to stay with them, but Izora refused to listen. She left the party and set out on her own to find a way to kill the wisteria dragon.

Izora's long isolation and many hostile encounters with other floral dragons turned her rage to simmering bitterness as she searched for their weaknesses. She came to believe that all floral dragons must be wiped out, not just the wisteria.

One day, Izora stumbled upon a dying {@creature Dandelion Dragon|FGoFD24} with mushrooms growing out of its head. Izora recognized the fungus as the pleurossa, a local fungus that decomposes floral dragon bodies after they die, but had never seen it growing from a live dragon before. Still fixated on killing the wisteria dragon, she wondered if the pleurossa could be weaponized against the floral dragons.

The sorcerer began to experiment with the pleurossa in a remote camp deep in the forest, corrupting the benign fungus with magic. Izora tested her creation on a {@creature Clematis Dragon|FGoFD24}. As the pleurossa consumed the dragon, the victim thrashed, cutting Izora with its razor-like petals. Enthralled by the dragon's transformation into a mindless host for the pleurossa, Izora paid no attention to her own wounds. Pleurossa spores entered her bloodstream through the gashes on her hands, and started the process of corrupting her as well.

Over the following weeks, Izora continued her experiments as she became weaker and weaker while the pleurossa progressed through her body. Eventually, she became so sick she could only lie on her cot, cursing the world that she wouldn't be able to complete her revenge. As she lay dying, Izora's thoughts were consumed by hatred for floral dragons. But the pleurossa was not only killing her—it was absorbing her. As Izora's consciousness merged with the pleurossa, she became aware of a vast, interconnected mycelial network growing just beneath the forest floor. Izora's hatred and fear of the floral dragons were so strong that as the pleurossa consumed her, it was fundamentally changed. The pleurossa grew a rudimentary consciousness fixated on completing Izora's goal of bringing an end to all floral dragons.

Within moments, Izora's body was gone, leaving only her urge for revenge which lived on inside the pleurossa. Enhanced by Izora's arcane power, the pleurossa grew a large fruiting body, the fearsome mushroom dragon. This monstrosity would be the pleurossa's weapon to execute Izora's undying wish to exterminate all floral dragons.

In the months that followed, Izora's corrupted pleurossa established itself in the forest, outcompeting the other fungi. The floral dragons living nearby soon fell to its {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24}, including the proud wisteria dragon that had destroyed Izora's village.

The pleurossa's progress is slow yet devastating, while the mushroom dragon causes massive destruction and spreads pleurossa spores that can corrupt all living creatures. All floral dragons that have encountered it know to beware the mushroom that moves.
Meanwhile, Izora's former friends had only the notes she left behind in her camp to try to piece together what happened to her and how she is connected to this new and looming threat.

{@style {@font Corruption changes the floral dragons. The playful dandelion dragon is reduced to a husk of itself. Its leafy tail and fluffy antennae are no more, and its eyes are hollow.|Zethandriel}|large}

{@style {@font The mushrooms that grow on its body and head are the same toxic ones that the pleurossa produces. Izora loved the dandelion dragons once; she was the one who told me about them in the first place.|Zethandriel}|large}

entries.name: Physiology
entries: There is only one corrupted pleurossa, a vast underground mycelial network spanning miles. Its web of mycelial threads enables the fungus to sense the position of creatures in its forest. Recent observations indicate that the pleurossa is still expanding and may even be growing another fruiting body like the mushroom dragon. There is no data on how old or large the network could become.
Sprouting from the pleurossa as mushrooms sprout from their mycelia, the mushroom dragon is an eight-legged monster with enormous fungal growths for wings and a veiny hole for a mouth.

Four sharp teeth line the top of its maw, with two more protruding from its bottom jaw. Its thick tail trails behind it, shedding spores to spread the pleurossa {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24}. Its spongey scales are broad and as thick as mushroom caps. The mushroom dragon is one with the pleurossa, and travels to areas where it can hunt and infect new hosts with the fungal infection. Its dragon-like form manifested from Izroa's fixation on floral dragons.

A few seconds' exposure to the airborne spores around the pleurossa or the mushroom dragon is enough for a host to become infected. The pleurossa also infects creatures through wounds or by being ingested, and slowly kills the host if left unchecked. Once the {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24} has progressed far enough, an infected host connects to the pleurossa, able to sense its surroundings through the mycelial network. As the {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24} continues, hosts become more interconnected with the pleurossa until, eventually, they are absorbed entirely. The vast network feeds on the body's nutrients and subsumes any remnant of the host's mind.
{@style {@font I heard reports of fouled water near the forest so I went to investigate. As I feared, the pleurossa still dwells within these woods.|Zethandriel}|large}

{@style {@font Its presence pollutes the area and makes it nigh uninhabitable. I wish I could have done more to stop it. I should never have let Izora go off alone after we found her village destroyed.|Zethandriel}|large}

entries.name: Habitat
entries: The pleurossa extends throughout the forest where it was corrupted by Izora. While the mushroom dragon can travel beyond this range, it is strongest when it is close to the mycelial network, which allows it to sense its environment far beyond its own meager perception.
Within the forest, spores produced by the pleurossa network and the dragon are an ever-present threat, giving the region a distinct musty smell.

Floral dragons that live in the forest are either hosts or soon-to-be hosts; none are immune to the infectious spores exuded by the mushroom dragon. Some creatures and plants on the outskirts of the pleurossa's territory guard the forest, defending against the spread of the {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24}, even as they risk succumbing to the mycelial network themselves.

{@style {@font The mushroom dragon is the living embodiment of hatred for floral dragons. I doubt the pleurossa would have been able to produce such a creature on its own. Izora's magic must have powered it somehow.|Zethandriel}|large}
{@style {@font I wonder if there is anything left of my friend in there… and if she can be saved.|Zethandriel}|large}

entries.name: Behavior
entries: The mushroom dragon and the pleurossa have no capacity for intelligent thought, only a primal need to destroy floral dragons.

Though the pleurossa can absorb any creature into the mycelial network, its natural role as a decomposer of floral dragon corpses, combined with Izora's hatred, causes it to corrupt floral dragons in unique ways. Whereas other corrupted creatures are eventually consumed by the pleurossa, floral dragons' petals wither and die, their forms contort, and their minds rot. A floral dragon that undergoes these changes eventually becomes a corrupted floral dragon.

The pleurossa is unrecognizable from its former role as a beneficial fungus. It is now a monster—single-minded and destructive. The pleurossa siphons nutrients from hosts it absorbs and uses the mushroom dragon to consume living things in its path. As the pleurossa cannot perceive its surroundings beyond the mycelial network's growth, it uses the mushroom dragon's capacity for flight to search for opportunities to expand beyond its territory. Wherever the mushroom dragon is sighted, the rest of the pleurossa is never far behind.
{@style {@font Under the effects of the corruption, infected floral dragons no longer need to eat because they share all nutrients with the pleurossa.|Zethandriel}|large}

{@style {@font The azalea dragon's tongue melts away, and mycelia root throughout its body. I never met an azalea dragon myself, but I vaguely remember Kaltaar telling me about them as I faded in and out of consciousness.|Zethandriel}|large}
{@style {@font He befriended a pack of them once.|Zethandriel}|large}

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: Here are ways to include the pleurossa fungus and mushroom dragon in your game.

rows: An elderly elf named Zethandriel [they/them] approaches the party for help. They have been trying to stop the pleurossa for decades and are in search of fresh ideas. They tell the party their friend Izora created the corrupted fungus and that she is likely lost forever.

A nomadic group sets up camp outside the pleurossa-infected forest. They send several people into the forest to gather food, but none return. The leader of the group asks the party to find their missing people.

Researchers captured a larkspur dragon with a single mushroom growing from its skull. They have quarantined it to learn what is wrong with it. The researchers hire the party to go into the forest and find the rest of the dragon's blooming. They are willing to pay generously and warn that the mushrooms are extremely dangerous

Winds from a storm carried pleurossa spores to a nearby village. All inhabitants of the village have gained some levels of {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24}. The mushroom dragon will claim the village as its territory and advance to nearby settlements if it is not stopped.

items.name: Ideal
entries: "All floral dragons are a threat to the world and must be wiped out."

items.name: Bond
entries: "We are all one: the mushroom dragon, the corrupted floral dragons, the network."

items.name: Flaw
entries: "I am corrupted by a dead sorcerer's hatred."

entries.name: The Pleurossa Network
entries: In combat, the pleurossa network is not a creature that can be attacked. It has a reserve of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} it can distribute to the {@creature mushroom dragon|FGoFD24} and corrupted floral dragons. At the start of combat, it has 50 hp in its reserve. This amount can be increased or decreased to change the difficulty of combat.

items.name: Gaining and Distributing Hit Points
entries: When corrupted creatures die, the pleurossa network gains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to a roll of the creature's hit dice. On initiative count 10 (losing ties) the pleurossa can distribute any number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to either one corrupted floral dragon of its choice or the {@creature mushroom dragon|source|optional text}, removing the same amount of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from its reserve.

items.name: Shared Perception
entries: The pleurossa can perceive the world around it through its network of fungal fibers that reach throughout the ground and through the corrupted floral dragons and the mushroom dragon. Corrupted floral dragons and the mushroom dragon can perceive everything the pleurossa does while they are within its area.

items.name: Destroying the Pleurossa Network
entries: The pleurossa network can't be attacked directly but can be destroyed. To destroy the pleurossa, it must die and be unable to regrow. Once the mushroom dragon has been defeated, the pleurossa has few defenses until it can grow a new one. During this time, it can be destroyed through any logical method with enough power and effort, such as fire, fungicide, or magic. Alternatively, if Izora's corrupting influence can be removed or calmed, the pleurossa will return to its former unthreatening state as a natural part of the ecosystem.

{@style {@font Just a whiff of the mushroom dragon's toxic breath is enough to make you sick with corruption. It is a cruel infection that results in a torturously slow death if left untreated.|Zethandriel}|large}
{@style {@font I am too old to do anything about it now, but if I publish these notes, they may reach someone who can.|Zethandriel}|large}

entries.name: Corrupted Floral Dragons
entries: When floral dragons and other creatures are infected by the pleurossa, they gain levels of {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24}, as detailed in the {@table Corruption Effects|FGoFD24} table. Floral dragons have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all saving throws made to resist {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24}. The infection slowly takes away their sense of self as they become one with the pleurossa.

Common signs of infection in floral dragons are decaying petals, visible bones, broken wings, and hollow eye sockets. Mushrooms sprout where flowers should be on an infected dragon's back, skull, and tail. If a floral dragon gains 6 levels of corruption, it becomes a {@b corrupted floral dragon}, as detailed in the {@area Corrupted Floral Dragon Template|172|x}. The {@creature corrupted azalea dragon|FGoFD24}, {@creature corrupted dandelion dragon|FGoFD24}, {@creature corrupted larkspur dragon|FGoFD24}, and {@creature corrupted wisteria dragon|FGoFD24} are provided as examples.

{@style {@font The changes that the corruption causes are perhaps most pronounced in the larkspur dragon. The dragon's song becomes an agonized screech, and signs of the mycelial network emerge all over its body and head.|Zethandriel}|large}
{@style {@font While we were just starting out, I was looking for the hydrangea dragon when Kaltaar found the larkspur dragon. I would have liked to have seen one in its prime.|Zethandriel}|large}

entries.name: Corrupted Floral Dragon Template
entries: When a floral dragon becomes a corrupted floral dragon, it retains its statistics with the following alterations. The GM decides if a corrupted floral dragon retains or loses any or all of its lair actions.

entries.name: Corrupted Traits
entries: All corrupted floral dragons share these traits:

items.name: Ideal
entries: "All floral dragons must be corrupted."

items.name: Bond
entries: "I am one with the pleurossa."

items.name: Flaw
entries: "I am singleminded in my hatred for floral dragons."

items.name: Altered Ability Scores
entries: The corrupted floral dragon's Intelligence becomes 3 (-4), its Wisdom becomes 12 (+1), and its Charisma becomes 4 (-3).

items.name: Resistances
entries: The corrupted floral dragon gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

items.name: Immunities
entries: The corrupted floral dragon gains {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage. The corrupted floral dragon can't be {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, or {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}. It also doesn't suffer from {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}.

items.name: Fungally Controlled
entries: The corrupted floral dragon is part of the pleurossa network. While it is within the pluerossa's area, it is aware of everything the pluerossa percieves. It carries out the desires of the pleurrosa without hesitation.

items.name: Senses
entries: The corrupted floral dragon gains {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} out to a range of 60 feet if it didn't already have it. It is blind beyond this radius and loses any other senses it had previously.

items.name: Speed
entries: The corrupted floral dragon gains a {@variantrule Burrow Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet. If the dragon has a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}, it is halved.

items.name: Languages
entries: The corrupted floral dragon can no longer understand or speak any language.

items.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The corrupted floral dragon has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

items.name: Melee Weapon Spores
entries: If the dragon has a melee weapon attack that deals piercing or slashing damage, on a hit a target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or gain one level of {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24}. The DC is equal to 8 + the dragon's proficiency bonus + the dragon's Constitution modifier. Floral dragons have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this saving throw.

items.name: Weakened
entries: The corrupted floral dragon can't cast spells or take legendary actions.

items.name: Floral Presence
entries: If the corrupted dragon had a Floral Presence before it was corrupted, it is replaced with the following feature with the range, damage, and saving throw determined by the original dragon's CR.

entries.name: Fungal Presence (Recharge of 5–6)
entries: The dragon exhales spores in a {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} originating from itself. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes Poison and Necrotic damage and gains a level of {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24}. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. If a target's saving throw is successful, the target is immune to the dragon's Fungal Presence for the next 24 hours. The Fungal Presence Strength table shows the ability's range, damage, and saving throw DC.

legendaryGroup.name: Aconite Dragon
lairActions: Aconite dragons lair in filthy swamps and marshes. While in its lair, an aconite dragon is empowered by the fetid conditions and has access to special actions.

lairActions.name: Lair Actions
entries: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects. The dragon can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The dragon exudes pheromones that react with the polluted water around it, producing a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of fog centered on a point the dragon chooses within 30 feet of it. The sphere's area is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB}. The fog disperses at the start of the dragon's next turn.

The dragon uses the foul bog water in the lair to overpower its foes. The dragon can target any number of creatures it sees in swamp water within 90 feet of it. A target must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Poison damage and be {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until the end of its next turn. A target in a boat or otherwise not in direct contact with the water has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw.

Corrupt vegetation growing in and around the swamp grasps all creatures in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} within 60 feet of the dragon that it can see. Each creature in the area must succeed on a {@dc 17} Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 20 feet into the water and knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}. A target in a boat or otherwise not in direct contact with the water has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw.

regionalEffects: The region containing an aconite dragon's lair is Poisoned by the dragon's presence, which creates one or more of the following effects:

items: Trees within 1 mile of the dragon's lair have white bark and gnarled branches.

Water sources within 1 mile of the dragon's lair are tainted with toxic drool, rendering it unsuitable for drinking, washing, or cooking. It cannot be boiled clean. The {@spell Purify Food and Drink|XPHB} spell removes the toxicity, but the water retains its sludgy viscosity.
The aconite flowers that grow within 1 mile of the dragon's lair make especially potent toxins.

regionalEffects: If the dragon dies, these effects fade over the course of {@dice 1d10} days.

legendaryGroup.name: Apple Tree Dragon
lairActions: The whole settlement that an apple tree dragon protects is considered its lair.

lairActions.name: Lair Actions
entries: While fighting in its lair, the apple tree dragon is empowered by love for its home. On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: An ally of the dragon within its lair gains {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB|inspiration}.
An ally of the dragon within its lair gains 6 ({@damage 2d10}) {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

Roots erupt from the ground in a 100-foot diameter circle centered on the dragon. All creatures within this area must succeed on a {@dc 20} Dexterity saving throw or drop {@condition Prone|XPHB}. The area becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.

regionalEffects: The region containing an apple dragon's lair is affected by the dragon's magic, which creates one or more of the following effects:

items: Crops grown within 10 miles of the lair are unnaturally fruitful and resistant to disease.
People tend to be less argumentative and more collaborative.
On rainy days, a rainbow can almost always be seen, arching toward the dragon.

regionalEffects: If the dragon dies, these effects fade over the course of {@dice 1d10} days.

legendaryGroup.name: Manchineel Dragon
lairActions: Any area a manchineel stays in is quickly corrupted and becomes its lair. The ground, water, and air fill with its acrid poison.

lairActions.name: Lair Actions
entries: While fighting in its lair, the manchineel dragon is empowered by its poisonous miasma. On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The dragon burrows up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. All creatures in its path or on the surface above its path must succeed on a {@dc 26} Dexterity saving throw or be knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}.
Manchineel plants in the lair drip toxic sap. Each creature in the lair must make a {@dc 25} Dexterity saving throw or take 21 ({@damage 6d6}) Acid damage, or half as much damage on a success.

Patches of ground within 90 feet of the dragon become unstable and crumble. Creatures in 20-foot square area of the dragon's choice must succeed on a {@dc 25} Dexterity saving throw or fall into a 20-foot-deep hole and take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Bludgeoning damage.

regionalEffects: The region containing a manchineel dragon's lair is warped by the dragon's magic, which creates one or more of the following effects:

items: When it rains, the area within 1 mile of the dragon's lair experiences acid rain.
The ground within 1 mile of the lair has large, deep holes from the dragon's burrowing.
Fruit and vegetables grown within 20 miles of the dragon's lair have an acidic aftertaste, though they are not poisonous themselves.

regionalEffects: If the dragon dies, these effects fade over the course of {@dice 1d10} days.

legendaryGroup.name: Peony Dragon
lairActions: Peony dragons make their lairs in earthen craters that they dig themselves, surrounded by tall peony flowers. They spend most of their time in the den caring for their blooming or hunting for food either in the field of peony flowers or nearby forests. A lair might be home to half a dozen adult peony dragons and their young.

lairActions.name: Lair Actions
entries: While fighting inside its lair, a peony dragon can make tactical use of its home environment to take lair actions. On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can't use the same effect two rounds in a row.

items: Tall peony flowers grow rapidly, hiding the dragon from sight. To discern the dragon's location, a creature can use its action to find it and must succeed on a {@dc 16} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check. While it remains hidden in this way, the dragon has half cover. These effects last until the dragon attacks or uses another lair action.

The dragon kicks up a cloud of dirt from its den. One creature of its choice within 5 feet of it must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or be {@condition Blinded|XPHB} until the start of the dragon's next turn.

Peony flowers twist and writhe on the ground, tripping enemies of the dragon. Each creature in a line 30 feet long and 5 feet wide originating from the dragon must succeed on a {@dc 14} Strength saving throw or be knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}.

regionalEffects: The area in the vicinity of a peony dragon's lair is influenced by the dragon's presence, which creates one or more of the following effects:

items: Unnaturally tall peonies bloom 10 feet high within 30 feet of the lair and gradually expand to overtake the surrounding grasslands.
Patches of grassland where the tall peonies are growing are {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.
The population of vespons in the area is much higher than normal. There is a notable absence of other pollinators.

regionalEffects: If all the dragons sharing the lair die or leave, these effects fade over the course of {@dice 2d6} months.

legendaryGroup.name: Succulent Dragon
lairActions: While in its lair, a succulent dragon can use its deep connection to the cacti that form its home to strengthen its defenses.

lairActions.name: Lair Actions
entries: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the dragon can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The living cactus fence lashes out. Each creature within 10 feet of the fence must make a {@dc 18} Strength saving throw. On a failure, it is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} (escape {@dc 18}). While {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, a creature takes 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Piercing damage at the start of each of its turns.

Cacti burst from the ground starting from a point that the dragon can see within 60 feet of it, creating a 25-foot long, 5-foot wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. Each creature in the line must make a {@dc 18} Dexterity Saving Throw, taking 12 ({@damage 5d4}) Piercing damage on a failed save and half as much on a success.

A tremor shakes the lair in a 30-foot radius around the dragon. Each creature on the ground in that area other than the dragon must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or be knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}.

regionalEffects: The region containing a legendary succulent dragon's lair is warped by the dragon's magic, which creates one or more of the following effects:

items: The succulent plants growing within 1 mile of the dragon's lair have regenerative properties. If they are severed or damaged, they regrow fully within {@dice 1d10} minutes.
There are frequent tremors within 1 mile of the dragon's lair.
The area within 1 mile of the dragon's lair is several degrees hotter than the ambient temperature outside this area, even at night.

regionalEffects: If the dragon dies, these effects fade over the course of {@dice 1d10} days.

legendaryGroup.name: The Pleurossa
lairActions: The pleurossa fully infests the forest where it merged with Izora. There is no place its mycelial tendrils do not reach. While the mushroom dragon is within its area, the pleurossa can take lair actions.

lairActions.name: Lair Actions
entries: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the pleurossa takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects; the pleurossa can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The pleurossa summons a {@filter corrupted floral dragon|bestiary|source=fgofd24|Challenge Rating=[&0;&4]|group=corrupted floral dragon|miscellaneous=!reprinted} of CR 4 or lower to aid the mushroom dragon in combat. Roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} for the corrupted floral dragon. The pleurossa can use this lair action twice per day.

Glittering spores fill the air in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube}. Each creature within that area must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or be affected as if by the {@spell Faerie Fire|XPHB} spell.

The {@area pleurossa network|164|x} unearths itself in a 20-foot radius centered on a point on the ground within 120 feet of the mushroom dragon. The area becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} and each creature in that area must succeed on a {@dc 19} Strength saving throw or be {@condition Restrained|XPHB} by roots until the pleurossa takes another lair action. A creature can be freed if it or another creature takes an action to make a {@dc 15} Strength check and succeeds.

regionalEffects: The region containing the pleurossa is warped by its presence, which creates one or more of the following effects:

items: Water sources within 5 miles of the lair are contaminated. A creature that drinks the water is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} for {@dice 1d4 + 1} hours after ingesting it.
Plants and animals appear sickly, and the forest is eerily silent as no birds sing here.
The mushrooms that grow in the forest are corrupted. A creature that ingests a mushroom must succeed on a {@dc 22} Constitution saving throw or gain one level of {@condition Corruption|FGoFD24}.

regionalEffects: If the pleurossa dies, these effects fade over the course of {@dice 1d10} days.

item.name: Floral Dragon Grooming Rake
entries: The firm prongs of this rake are designed to remove dead leaves, wilted flowers, and dirt from a floral dragon. When you spend 10 minutes using this rake to groom a willing floral dragon, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) checks made to interact with the floral dragon for the next 24 hours. Additionally, the dragon makes all Dexterity and Constitution saving throws with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} for the next 24 hours.

item.name: Cherry Blossom Token
entries: Made from a pressed flower from the cherry blossom dragon, this token can bring good fortune.

While carrying this token, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Performance|XPHB} checks made to tell stories. Additionally, when you fail an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the d20 and must use the new result. Once you have used this property, you can't use it again until next dusk.

item.name: Clematis Poison
entries: A creature subjected to the poison must make a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw, taking 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails its save is also {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} for 1 hour.
This poison has no effect on creatures that are immune to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

item.name: Great Harvest Apple
entries: This enormous apple is produced by an apple tree dragon. The apple is large enough to provide up to ten creatures with sustenance for one day. The apple can be sliced and shared, hollowed out and used for cooking, or baked into other dishes. A creature that spends at least 10 minutes consuming part of the apple gains the following benefits:

items: It gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the number of creatures that also consumed part of the apple during the same meal.
It gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid damage for the next 24 hours.

entries: A creature can only benefit from a great harvest apple's effects once every 24 hours.

item.name: Hydrangea Dragon Antidote
entries: This viscous liquid shifts between blue and pink in its vial. It is brewed from the blooms of a living hydrangea dragon.

A creature that has been poisoned that drinks this vial of liquid is no longer {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}. It also regains {@dice 2d12} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and reduces its levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} by 3.

item.name: Hydrangea Dragon Poison
entries: This colorless poison is harvested from the blooms of a living hydrangea dragon. A creature subjected to this poison must make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 4d12} Poison damage, gains 4 levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}, and has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until it is treated with {@item Hydrangea Dragon Antidote|FGoFD24}. On a successful save, the creature gains 2 levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} and isn't {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}.

item.name: Ornithogalum Dragon Elixir
entries: This shimmering, translucent green liquid is distilled from a living ornithogalum dragon's flowers. When you drink this potion, your {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level is reduced by one. Additionally, you can spend {@variantrule Hit Dice|XPHB} as though you had taken a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

item.name: Peony Dragon Essence
entries: This fragrant essence is made from the tall peonies in a peony dragon's lair and is popular among spellcasters. Each vial of peony dragon essence contains {@dice 1d4 + 2} doses. When you cast an abjuration spell, you can add the essence to the spell as a material component to improve one casting of the spell with one of the following benefits:

items: For 1 minute, the spell does not require {@status Concentration|XPHB}.
You gain a +1 bonus to the spell attack roll or spell save DC of the spell.
You can choose one additional target for the spell.

item.name: Succulent Water of Life
entries: This thin liquid is light green but becomes dark red when shaken. When you drink this potion, you regain {@dice 1d10} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and for 1 minute, you regain {@dice 1d10} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of each of your turns, provided you have at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point}.

item.name: Ornithogalum Dragon Honey
entries: This thick liquid tastes sweet with a hint of herbal notes. One hour after consuming this honey, you must make a {@dc 19} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, you suffer a level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}.

item.name: Wisteria Dragon Perfume
entries: This light purple translucent perfume is sealed in a glass orb. As an action, you can throw the orb up to 60 feet away from you, shattering it on impact and releasing a powerful scent of wisteria flowers that spreads out in a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on the point orb shattered. The sphere of invisible perfume spreads around corners and lasts for {@dice 1d4} rounds. Each creature that starts its turn inside the sphere or enters it on its turn must succeed on a {@dc 19} Constitution saving throw or fall {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} for 1 minute. Floral dragons, except for wisteria dragons, have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this saving throw. The effect ends for an affected creature if it takes any damage.

item.name: Dandelion Hourglass
entries: Fluffy seeds from {@creature dandelion dragon|FGoFD24|dandelion dragons} drift between the two bulbs of this hourglass. While attuned to this item, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls. Additionally, when a creature you can see within 120 feet of you rolls {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force it to make a {@dc 15} Intelligence saving throw. A creature can choose to fail the save. On a failure, the target must reroll its {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and must use the new result. Once you have used this property, you can’t use it again until the next dawn.

This weapon is coated in the powerful toxin of a clematis dragon. When you hit with this weapon, the target must make a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 1d8} Poison damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature that fails its save is also {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} until the end of its next turn unless it is immune to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. Once a creature has been {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} by this weapon, it is immune to the weapon's paralyzing effects for the next 24 hours.

magicvariant.name: Armor of the Vampire Lily Dragon

entries: This armor has been reinforced with the spines of a {@creature Vampire Lily Dragon|FGoFD24}. You have a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor. Additionally, a creature that {@condition grappled|XPHB|grapples} you or hits you with a melee attack while within 5 feet of you must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d6} Poison damage and become {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until the end of its next turn.

condition.name: Corruption
entries: The mushroom dragon and the pleurossa network can infect creatures with corruption. This disease turns creatures into hosts, slowly kills them, and absorbs them into the pleurossa network. The infection can be obtained by inhaling toxic spores, sustaining injury, or ingesting corrupted organic material. Wearing a face covering grants {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against corruption through inhalation, and wearing adamantine armor grants advantage on saving throws against corruption through injury. Constructs and undead are immune to corruption.

entries.name: Effects
entries: Corruption is measured in six levels. The {@table Corruption Effects|FGoFD24} table shows the consequences of each level of corruption. A creature suffers the effects of its current level of corruption as well as all lower levels. A floral dragon that gains six levels of corruption becomes a corrupted floral dragon.

entries.name: Progression of Corruption
entries: On its own, corruption progresses slowly. Once every {@deck 2d12} days, a creature with at least 1 level of corruption must make a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature gains a level of corruption. Repeated exposure to the spores or the attacks of corrupted floral dragons can rapidly increase corruption.

entries.name: Death While Corrupted
entries: When a creature with one or more levels of corruption dies, it is absorbed into the pleurossa. The pleurossa network gains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to a roll of the creature’s {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice}, which become part of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} reserve.

entries.name: Ending the Corruption
entries: Corruption lasts until all levels of corruption are removed by a {@spell Greater Restoration|XPHB} spell or similar magic

entries.name: Temporary Immunity
entries: Once a creature has removed all levels of corruption, it is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to corruption for the next 24 hours.

rows.name: Infected
entries: The creature is {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}. This level can be removed if, within 8 hours of infection, the creature is subject to the {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB} spell or an item that cures the poisoned condition.

rows.name: Mild
entries: The creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Constitution saving throws.

rows.name: Moderate
entries: The mushroom dragon can see through the creature’s eyes. The creature is {@condition Blinded|XPHB} with regard to its own senses and gains {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} out to a range of 10 feet.

rows.name: Advanced
entries: Each time the creature takes damage, it takes an extra 3 Necrotic damage.

rows.name: Severe
entries: At the start of each of the creature’s turns, it must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it can either move, take an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, or take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

rows.name: Complete Corruption
entries: The creature dies and becomes one with the pleurossa. The pleurossa network gains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to a roll of the creature’s {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice}. Only a {@spell True Resurrection|XPHB} or {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell or divine intervention can restore the creature to life. Alternatively, if the creature is a floral dragon, it becomes a {@filter corrupted floral dragon|bestiary|source=fgofd24|group=corrupted floral dragon|miscellaneous=!reprinted} as detailed in the Corrupted Floral Dragon Template.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Flowers
entries: The first druids of the Circle of Flowers were people who sought out and bonded with floral dragons. The druids learned how to imitate floral dragons' forms and unique existence as beings that blend plants and animals. Now, these druids protect the floral dragons who first inspired their circle as well as the balance of nature in both its beauty and ferocity.

subclassFeature.name: Floral Form
entries: Your body begins a transformation as you take on plant-like aspects, such as flowers blooming from your head or your skin becoming bark-like. You gain different benefits depending on the type of flower you choose. Once you gain access to a floral form spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

entries.caption: Floral Form
rows: Aconite, clematis, larkspur
You always have the {@spell Detect Poison and Disease|XPHB} spell prepared and gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage.
Amaranth, apple tree, jade vine, magnolia

You always have the {@spell Goodberry|XPHB} spell prepared, and whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to a creature, the creature regains {@damage 1d4} additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Azalea, hydrangea, peony, succulent
You always have the {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB} spell prepared, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Saving Throws to resist being {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}.
Cherry blossom, dandelion, heliconia, wisteria
You always have the {@spell Sleep|XPHB} spell prepared, and magic can't put you to sleep.
Lamium, water lily
You always have the {@spell Create or Destroy Water|XPHB} spell prepared and gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your base walking speed.
Rhododendron, ornithogalum, manchineel, vampire lily
You always have the {@spell Bane|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to {@action Dash|XPHB} toward a hostile creature.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Wild Shape
entries: Your intimacy with the floral dragons lets you take on their forms. You add the following floral dragon shapes to your beast shapes that you can use with your {@classFeature Wild Shape|Druid|XPHB|2|XPHB} feature, ignoring any restrictions based on CR, swim speed, or fly speeds.

subclassFeature.name: Dendrology Defenses
entries: As your connection with flowers deepens, you take on more plant-like traits. You can cast the {@spell Barkskin|XPHB} spell on yourself once a day without expending a spell slot. Additionally, when you cast {@spell Barkskin|XPHB} you don't need to concentrate on the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Flower Circle
entries: Your connection with flowers lets you summon them from the earth to soothe yourself and your companions. During a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short Rest}, you can cause an area of flowers to bloom on the ground in a 15-foot radius centered on you that lasts for 1 hour, until you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or you leave the circle. Creatures of your choice within the area gain the following benefits:

items: When they regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} by spending Hit Dice or with magic, they regain additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. Creatures can only benefit from this once per {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short Rest}.
If they spend the full hour resting in the circle, they gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage for 8 hours.

entries: Once you have used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Full Bloom
entries: Your flowery transformation begins to include draconic features as the magic of the floral dragons runs through your veins like sap. You gain new benefits based on the flower of your Floral Form.

entries.caption: Full Bloom
rows: Aconite, clematis, larkspur
Your melee weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d8} Poison damage on a hit, and you gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison damage.
Amaranth, apple tree, magnolia
You always have the {@spell Heroes' Feast|XPHB} spell prepared and can cast it without the need for material components once every ten days.
Azalea, hydrangea, peony, succulent
Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to a creature, the creature regains additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@damage 1d8 + 5}.
Cherry blossom, wisteria
You always have the {@spell Etherealness|XPHB} spell prepared and can cast it once a day without expending a spell slot.
Lamium, water lily
Your {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} is double your base walking speed, you can breathe underwater, and you gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage.
Rhododendron, manchineel, vampire lily

You always have the {@spell Mordenkainen's Sword|XPHB|Arcane Sword} spell prepared, which takes the form of razor-sharp swirling leaves and petals. You can cast it without the need for material components.
Dandelion, heliconia, ornithogalum, jade vine
Wings sprout from your back, and you gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your walking speed.

subclassFeature.name: Field Researcher
entries: Field Researcher Rangers investigate and protect the natural world. These explorers seek to preserve and understand the magic of floral dragons. Their skills let them roam wherever their research requires, and their observational abilities make them formidable opponents and steadfast allies should danger arise.

subclassFeature.name: Field Researcher Magic
entries: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Field Researcher Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Case Study
entries: Your focus in combat lets you find the perfect moment to strike again. When you hit a creature with an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make another attack with the same weapon against that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Research Skills
entries: You have honed your research abilities, making you adaptable in the field. Whenever you make an Intelligence check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).
In addition, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill History|XPHB}, {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, or {@skill Nature|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Research Team
entries: You have learned that working with a group is key to successful field research. When you are adjacent to an ally, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to grant your ally {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on one attack roll or skill check they make on their turn.

subclassFeature.name: Hands-on Analysis
entries: Your ability to handle wild creatures lets you deal with those that might be hostile to others. When you cast the spells {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB}, {@spell Animal Messenger|XPHB}, {@spell Conjure Animals|XPHB}, {@spell Locate Animals or Plants|XPHB}, or {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB}, you can target or summon Plants and Dragons as well as Beasts as long as all the other requirements of the spell are met.

Additionally, when you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to a Plant or Dragon, the creature regains additional {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

subclassFeature.name: Floral Collaboration
entries: Thanks to your extensive research, you know exactly what to call on for aid. You can cast {@spell Summon Dragon|XPHB} without a Material component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you cast this spell, you can choose to summon a {@filter floral dragon|bestiary|Challenge Rating=[&0;&5]|group=floral dragon|miscellaneous=!reprinted} or {@filter Plant|bestiary|Challenge Rating=[&0;&5]|type=plant|miscellaneous=!reprinted} of CR 5 or lower instead of a {@creature Draconic Spirit|XPHB|Dragon spirit}. When you summon a floral dragon, you can choose to make Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) checks instead of Constitution saving throws to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB} on this spell.

subclassFeature.name: Fungus
entries: You have entered into a pact with a great Fungus, intertwining your life with it in exchange for power. The Fungus is a strange entity, neither animal nor vegetable. Tying your life to it changes you in peculiar ways as your body becomes a substrate for its mycelium.

The alien will of the fungus is difficult to comprehend, but the deeper you go down this path, the more it makes sense. Fungi may wish to grow and expand, revitalize the environment through decay, or carry out some other strange design. You may have tied yourself to a Fungus that is part of the natural cycle of life and death. Or perhaps you have given yourself over to the corrupted Pleurossa, taking on its vengeful mission to eradicate the floral dragons.

subclassFeature.name: Fungus Expanded Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Fungus Expanded Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Spread the Network
entries: Your spells leave an invisible trail connecting your targets to you and each other in a fragile network. When you damage a creature with a spell, you can add the target to your network for 1 minute or until your {@status Concentration|XPHB} is broken (as if you are concentrating on a spell). When you damage a creature in your network with a spell, you can deal {@damage 1d4} Necrotic damage to all other creatures in your network as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You can have a number of creatures in your network equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. When a creature dies, it is no longer part of your network. The damage you deal to creatures in your network increases to {@damage 2d4} when you reach 10th level in this class and {@damage 3d4} when you reach 17th level in this class.

subclassFeature.name: Mushroom Scouts
entries: You gain the ability to sprout watchful mushrooms. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can create a mushroom on a surface you can touch. You decide the appearance and type of mushroom when you create it. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can telepathically hear everything that the mushroom hears across any distance as long as you are on the same plane of existence. This effect lasts until the mushroom is destroyed or you sever the connection (no action required). You can have a number of mushrooms equal to your Charisma modifier active at one time.

subclassFeature.name: Seeing Unseen Threads
entries: Your interconnectedness with the great unseen network of the Fungus grows deeper. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage and {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 15 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Cycle of Decay
entries: You gain vigor from decomposition. Whenever you deal Necrotic damage to a creature, you gain {@damage 2d6} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Floral Breath Weapon
entries: Your dragonborn breath weapon blossoms out with the power of flowers. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an exhalation of swirling magical petals in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. Each creature in that area must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your Charisma modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 1d8} magical slashing damage and triggers the breath weapon effect of your Floral Legacy, as shown in the Floral Breath Weapon table. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and your breath weapon effect is not triggered. This damage increases by {@damage 1d8} when you reach character levels 5 ({@damage 2d8}), 11 ({@damage 3d8}), and 17 ({@damage 4d8}).

You can use your Floral Breath Weapon a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

raceFluff.name: Floral Dragonborn
entries: Blending the beauty of flowers and the ferocity of dragons, floral dragonborns take after the mysterious and majestic floral dragons. Rather than the bold metallic or chromatic scales of their dragonborn kin, their coloring evokes the delicate or vibrant shades of flowers, and they share as many traits with plants as they do with dragons.

entries.name: Wild Seeds
entries: The first floral dragonborn emerged long ago as infants born to dragonborn parents. From the moment of their birth, it is clear that floral dragonborns are different from their dragonborn kin. As they grow to adulthood, their plantlike nature becomes more obvious—buds, blossoms, and leaves begin to sprout, mimicking the flowery frills and manes of floral dragons. They come to resemble the floral dragon they take after far more than their own parents.

What causes a floral dragonborn to be born is hotly debated. Some believe that parents spending a lot of time around a floral dragon is enough to infuse an unborn child with a floral essence. Others think that eating certain plants or vespon honey can influence their birth. The existence of floral dragonborn who take after elusive or antisocial floral dragons indicates that whatever the cause, proximity is not always necessary. Today, enough generations have passed since they first began to appear that many floral dragonborn are also born to floral dragonborn parents. Depending on their dragonborn clan and the type of flower the infant takes after, the arrival of a floral dragonborn child may be celebrated as a sign of good fortune or a sign or an omen of disaster.

entries.name: Call of Nature
entries: Floral dragonborns are shaped by the cultures they grow up within. However, they also experience a deep sense of belonging and interconnectedness to natural environments. As living bridges between the three worlds of plants, dragons, and humanoids, many floral dragonborns feel a responsibility to maintain the balance between them.

The plant-like nature of floral dragonborns can also influence their personalities and attitudes. Just as trees and flowers change with the seasons, floral dragonborns can find themselves becoming restful in winter, energetic in spring, creative in summer, and somber in fall. They can also be particularly sensitive to pollution and changes in the environment.

entries.name: Floral Dragonborn Names
entries: Floral dragonborn draw their names from a variety of cultures, particularly draconic heritage. It is also common for them to receive names that speak to their connection with plants. As the first floral dragonborns were born into other dragonborn clans, early floral dragonborn clans weren’t based on family ties. Though these clans have become more established over time, they still gladly adopt floral dragonborns who seek a place to set down roots. Some floral dragonborn reject the clan system entirely, preferring to go wherever the wind blows them.

entries.name: Kin Wald
entries: I'm certain I'm not alone in having a childhood where fantasy was my medium for coping with the confusing world around me. I spent hundreds of hours curled up with the Dragonology books, meticulously copying each and every sketch, my childhood imagination running wild with the idea of a world filled with dragons.

When I first began creating floral dragons, it was the same cozy, childlike wonder I felt for those fantasy worlds that I tried to harness. For each of my creatures, I scrawl out ideas until I find some that make me smile—whether the design is cute, silly, or kind of nasty. My biggest goal with my art will always be to make others feel.

So, when people began to reach out about my floral dragon concepts and tell me of their potential in the realm of tabletop roleplaying games, I realized that I had an opportunity to expand the world and feelings of floral dragons even further. I wanted to give others the same kind of joy I felt creating these creatures. Roleplaying games are the perfect way to forget the worries of life for a few hours. The stories we tell let us stretch ourselves, feel emotions intensely, and think creatively. Though the worlds we play in are fantastical, the friendships we forge with our fellow players are real. To bring my floral dragons to this medium—to be a part of the catharsis and escapism of storytelling and roleplaying—has been an honor for me.

I decided to take a chance. I messaged Hit Point Press to pitch my floral dragons. Hit Point Press was my first choice of publisher as I was right in the middle of a Humblewood campaign. I was, and am, in love with Humblewood. Thinking of how happy the setting made me and how the art and lore created a wonderfully cozy escape for me and my friends in hard times, I knew Hit Point Press were the right people to help me bring my floral dragons to game tables. I got to work with this wonderful team to create these dragons and bring their world to life. I can't even begin to express my gratitude.

I hope that the bouquet of beasts within these pages make you smile and shudder. May the time you spend with them and the stories you tell with them will bring you excitement and laughter. Thank you for welcoming my creations to your table. I am ecstatic for the opportunity to share the world of the floral dragons with you.
{@i Creator and Illustrator}
{@i @kintheartist}

data.name: Introduction
entries: Welcome to {@i The Field Guide to Floral Dragons}, your guide to dragons imbued with the essence of flowers. With their abundant blooms and specialized physiology, floral dragons can be beautiful. However, any wise forager or florist knows that some plants can be as deadly as they are gorgeous.

Like plants, floral dragons are deeply connected to the land and weather in their habitat; like dragons, their temperaments range from docile to dangerous. A group of floral dragons found in the wild is known as a "blooming."

There are many ways to include floral dragons in your games. Some floral dragons are friendly; they need the party's help, or make excellent companions. Others are malicious; the party may be tasked with subduing or stopping them from causing havoc.

Floral dragons thrive in a variety of environments and can blossom in your existing game setting. You can also use the descriptions of the dragons' habitats to create an original setting for a campaign, a world blooming with magic.

In these pages, you'll find tales of the floral dragons' origins, information about their habitat, and details of relationships with humanoids and other floral dragons. You'll also find plot hooks to introduce them to your players and tables of personality traits and motivations to make the dragons your own.

entries.name: Safety at the Table
entries: Before you introduce floral dragons to your players, discuss as a group which themes you want to engage with and which you'd rather leave out. The {@i Field Guide to Floral Dragons} contains the following themes:
There may also be other themes that don't work for your table. Read the book carefully and talk with your players to create an experience you can all enjoy.

Safety tools such as lines and veils can help to guide this conversation. Lines and veils are a framework to establish boundaries before the game begins. A line is a topic that will not show up in the game at all. A veil is a topic that may be referred to in the game but will not be explored in detail. For more safety tool options, take a look at the TTRPG Safety Toolkit. The TTRPG Safety Toolkit is a free resource co-curated by Kienna Shaw and Lauren Bryant-Monk. It is a compilation of safety tools designed by members of the tabletop roleplaying games community for use by players and GMs at the table. You can find it online at {@i bit.ly/ttrpgsafetytoolkit}.

entries.name: How to Use This Book
entries: {@i The Field Guide to Floral Dragons} is designed to be used with the 5e Core Rules. Throughout, magic items and spells appear in {@i italics}, and new magic items are marked with an asterisk {@sup *}. Creatures with game statistics in {@i The Field Guide to Floral Dragons} appear in {@b bold} when relevant. The book is divided into three sections:

First, the floral dragons are presented alphabetically, except where floral dragons with connected stories are grouped together. You'll also find new magic items associated with floral dragons throughout this section.
The next section gives the details of other creatures that live alongside floral dragons, including their pests, pollinators, and the vengeful {@b pluerossa fungus}.
Finally, at the back of the book, you'll find a guide to creatures in this book by Challenge Rating (CR) and indexes of magic items and creatures.

entries.name: Field Notes
entries: The field notes throughout this book were written by four different members of an adventuring party determined to learn as much as they could about floral dragons of all kinds. The party's research led them to a terrible threat—the {@book pleurossa fungus|FGoFD24|22}. Piecing together the field notes tells the story of the party's discoveries and how the actions of one of them led to the {@creature Mushroom Dragon|FGoFD24|mushroom dragon's} creation.

items: {@style {@font Handwriting like this belongs to Amina [she/they], an orc bard|Amina}|large}.
{@style {@font Handwriting like this belongs to Kaltaar [he/him], a dragonborn druid.|Kaltaar}|large}
{@style {@font Handwriting like this belongs to Izora [she/her], a human sorcerer.|Izora}|large}
{@style {@font Handwriting like this belongs to Zethandriel [they/them], an elf barbarian.|Zethandriel}|large}

entries: {@style {@font To whoever finds these humble notes, may they bring you enlightenment and a warning.|Zethandriel}|large}

{@style {@font My friends and I investigated the wonderous creatures known as floral dragons. We found fragrant marvels, astonishing blooms, and true friendships. But we also found dangers deadlier than nightshade. I have gathered our notes and sketches here, hoping that others can learn from what we've seen.|Zethandriel}|large}

{@style {@font Do not do as we did and meddle with the creeping fungus! It's likely too late for us, but I still have hope. People and floral dragons can yet live in harmony. Perhaps even with the mushroom...|Zethandriel}|large}
{@style {@font Aconite dragons grow bioluminescent lures from their large heads.|Amina}|large}

entries.name: The Accidental Aconite Dragon
entries: Legends say that the first {@creature aconite dragon|FGoFD24} was the creation of a young bog witch called Lilura. Although Lilura had a domesticated toad that she loved, she wanted a more powerful companion who could help with her magic. Lilura took the extract of aconite flowers and combined it with a thickening agent, fetid water from her swamp, and a pinch of forbidden magic to create a potion.

Lilura fed the concoction to her beloved toad, hoping that it would enhance the toad's latent magic. The toad couldn't withstand the Poison and began to die. A panicked Lilura hurriedly cast a spell to change it into a creature that could tolerate the toxin. Rushed, the first thing that came to mind was a dragon. The spell worked, but the dragon was unlike any other Lilura had ever seen. It retained the petals of the aconite flower and grew huge, sharp teeth from a mouth dripping with thick saliva. Bioluminescent lures hung over its head and back.

When Lilura took her altered companion outside, it thrashed around, spraying drool everywhere, before hopping into the water. Though Lilura never saw it emerge during the daytime again, every night she loyally watched out of her window for the dragon's glowing lures so she could throw food into the swamp for it.

Influenced by the dragon's presence, the bog's Poisonous aconite flowers were forever tainted; they took on strange, new magical properties, inspiring Lilura to learn the art of Poisons. As her abilities as a Poison master grew, so did the swamp's aconite dragon population as she transformed more toads for the joy of watching their strange glow and the fear they inspired in others.

entries.name: Physiology

entries.title: {@style {@font Fig. 1 An aconite dragon waits against a tree, its lure glowing to attract prey.|Amina}|large}

entries: Aconite dragons are hulking creatures with wide mouths and thick, muscular limbs. Among its most notable features are the three bioluminescent lures that hang over its head and back to attract prey in the dark. The feet of an aconite dragon are webbed, and its suckered toes allow it to adhere to trees and wait for prey. Its flowers bloom in shades of purple. A thin layer of slime coats the dragon's skin to keep it from drying out when it isn't submerged in water. This slime is exuded from glands on its back, which are mottled light green. Young aconite dragons are darkest in color; older dragons become lighter as they age.

Most aconite dragons are around nine feet long and live between 150 and 200 years. Female aconite dragons are larger and heavier than males and are capable of growing up to three heads. These heads only grow on the most bloodthirsty aconite dragons; a female dragon must consume several other aconite dragons to grow another head. These three-headed dragons are known as {@creature greater aconite dragon|FGoFD24|greater aconite dragons}.

Aconite dragons have two hearts, one inside their chests and one in their bulbous heads. The second heart-like structure in its head circulates a tarry substance called ikvor instead of blood, pumping the black fluid throughout its body and to its huge maw. This deadly ikvor is a paralytic and Poisonous agent the dragon secretes through the roof of the mouth and into tiny canals in the teeth. An aconite dragon constantly drools this mixture, coating its prey in such vast quantities that the toxin can't be easily washed off, even in the dragon's boggy habitat. Greater aconite dragons have ikvor-hearts in all three of their heads.

{@style {@font I was walking around a marsh with Zethandriel, who told me not to stray off the path. I followed their instructions, but then I saw the prettiest light and couldn't stop myself from going toward it.|Amina}|large}
{@style {@font When I was close enough to see what I was looking at, I realized it was this giant, awful, frog-mutant thing! Gross!|Amina}|large}

{@style {@font Zethandriel said it was an aconite dragon, one of the floral dragons we are researching. And I thought all floral dragons were pretty! I won't be making that mistake again.|Amina}|large}

entries.name: Habitat
entries: Aconite dragons dwell in marshes, bogs, and swamps. They favor cooler temperatures and areas with plenty of dense trees. Despite their size, aconite dragons are agile climbers and hide in large trees to ambush prey. A tree repeatedly exposed to the aconite dragon's toxic drool will die, but not before its bark is bleached white and its boughs are gnarled by the Poisonous substance.

{@creature Clematis dragon|FGoFD24|Clematis dragons} are often found near the dwellings of aconite dragons; aconite dragons are immune to the toxins of the smaller, frog-like dragons and devour them as a vital food source. Aconite dragons often lay their clutches of eggs near a body of water where a clematis dragon has laid their eggs so their ravenous young have an easy first meal.

Whereas clematis dragons naturally cleanse swamps and marshes over time, aconite dragons pollute them. Algae growing in the bog occupied by an aconite dragon gradually turns a pale green to match the patches on the dragon's back, and aconite flowers spring up in the surrounding area. A few drops of an aconite dragon's drool is enough to contaminate a whole marsh.

entries.name: Behavior

entries.title: {@style {@font Fig. 2 An aconite dragon shows off its plumage and the slime glands on its back.|Amina}|large}

entries: Aconite dragons eat all manner of prey. As powerful apex predators, they tend to overhunt and will eat each other if they run out of other food. It's unusual for a bog to be home to more than one aconite dragon unless it has an uncommonly large and fast-growing population of creatures like deer, newts, or clematis dragons that the aconites can prey on.
During the daytime, aconite dragons stay submerged underwater, leaving only their lures visible above the surface.

Though they are mostly inactive in daylight, the dragon will take the opportunity to feed if a tasty source of food comes within striking distance. Otherwise, it hunts at night. It climbs trees and dangles its lure to attract prey. Once the prey is close enough, the aconite dragon spits its toxic drool on it, paralyzing the creature and giving the dragon time to kill it whenever it likes.

Once every few years, a female aconite dragon emits a sound at a frequency undetectable to humanoids to attract male dragons to her bog. She mates with the first one to find her and, once they have finished, will eat him if he is too slow to leave. Aconite dragon eggs incubate for around six months; the young are independent from the time they hatch. If their mother's bog has a plentiful source of prey, the young dragons compete for residence in other areas of the same bog; otherwise, they must find another body of water to live in.

Aconite dragons unable to find a suitable swamp have been known to settle in clean, exposed bodies of water, quickly turning them into their favored habitat. This habit can cause massive problems for the humanoid settlements that depend on the water polluted by the dragon. Aconite dragons rarely leave their homes; if they eat humanoids, it's usually because a lost humanoid wandered into an aconite dragon's territory or otherwise fell victim to the dragon's bioluminescent lure.

entries.caption: Aconite Dragon Personality Traits
rows: I eat only the crunchiest of clematis dragons.
There's nothing more satisfying than enticing unsuspecting prey with my lure.
I climb trees slowly by putting one toe on the trunk at a time.
I have yet to find something my bite can't snap in half.
I've been seeing the same mate for decades, and she hasn't eaten me—yet.
The marsh may be big enough for several aconite dragons, but I was here first and I won't let anyone forget it.
Nobody gets to touch my favorite tree.
My three heads frequently disagree with each other.

entries.caption: Aconite Dragon Motivations
rows: My lure is dull, and I want to find a way to make it brighter.
I won't rest until every body of water for miles around is a filthy bog.
Clematis dragons are a bane, and it is my job to cull them.
I'm bored of hunting weaker prey. I want a challenge.
I must eat other aconite dragons to grow two more heads.
I tasted humanoid flesh once, and I crave more.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: Here are ways to include aconite dragons in your game.

rows: An alchemist went missing after an expedition to collect aconite flowers from a toxic bog. They haven't been seen since, and the scouts who went searching for them have also not returned.
Villagers tell of a divine light that appears each night across the marsh. They worship it, believing it to be a local deity, and are planning a pilgrimage to find its source.
A group of researchers claims to have found a rare three-headed dragon and plan to capture it for study.

An entrepreneur has been illegally breeding aconite dragons in a remote bog, hoping to start a clematis dragon pest management service. He now has three large, hungry aconite dragons that he can't control.

entries: {@style {@font There was no way to continue through the marsh except to sneak around the dragon. It had its back to us, and I thought we'd gotten away when it turned and looked right at me!|Amina}|large}
{@style {@font It had thick black drool dripping from its jaws and its back was covered in slime. It's almost as bad as the vampire lily dragon. I'll be glad to leave this place.|Amina}|large}

entries.name: Greater Aconite Dragon
entries: A {@creature greater aconite dragon|FGoFD24} uses the same statistics as a regular {@creature aconite dragon|FGoFD24} with the following changes:

items: It makes three bite attacks using Multiattack.
Its bite attacks deal 21 ({@dice 3d10 + 5}) Piercing damage plus 4 ({@dice 1d8}) Poison damage.
It has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: An Aconite Dragon's Lair
entries: Aconite dragons lair in filthy swamps and marshes. While in its lair, an aconite dragon is empowered by the fetid conditions and has access to special actions.

entries.name: Lair Actions
entries: On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects. The dragon can't use the same effect two rounds in a row:

items: The dragon exudes pheromones that react with the polluted water around it, producing a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of fog centered on a point the dragon chooses within 30 feet of it. The sphere's area is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB}. The fog disperses at the start of the dragon's next turn.

The dragon uses the foul bog water in the lair to overpower its foes. The dragon can target any number of creatures it sees in swamp water within 90 feet of it. A target must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Poison damage and be {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until the end of its next turn. A target in a boat or otherwise not in direct contact with the water has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw.

Corrupt vegetation growing in and around the swamp grasps all creatures in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} within 60 feet of the dragon that it can see. Each creature in the area must succeed on a {@dc 17} Strength saving throw or be pulled up to 20 feet into the water and knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}. A target in a boat or otherwise not in direct contact with the water has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw.

entries.name: Regional Effects
entries: The region containing an aconite dragon's lair is Poisoned by the dragon's presence, which creates one or more of the following effects:

items: Trees within 1 mile of the dragon's lair have white bark and gnarled branches.

Water sources within 1 mile of the dragon's lair are tainted with toxic drool, rendering it unsuitable for drinking, washing, or cooking. It cannot be boiled clean. The {@spell Purify Food and Drink|XPHB} spell removes the toxicity, but the water retains its sludgy viscosity.
The aconite flowers that grow within 1 mile of the dragon's lair make especially potent toxins.

entries: If the dragon dies, these effects fade over the course of {@dice 1d10} days.
{@style {@font I thought these things couldn't get any worse! Apparently, these dragons can grow up to three heads—if one wasn't bad enough.|Amina}|large}
{@style {@font This three-headed dragon was much bigger than the others and three times as terrifying.|Amina}|large}
{@style {@font Forget the vampire lily; THIS is my least favorite floral dragon I've seen so far.|Amina}|large}

entries.title: {@style {@font Fig. 3 Triple-headed greater aconite dragons are a rare sight.|Amina}|large}

entries: {@style {@font Amaranth dragons are lively companions and excellent trackers.|Amina}|large}

entries.name: How the Amaranth Dragon Became a Friend
entries: The {@creature amaranth dragon|FGoFD24|amaranth dragons} were once immortal, or so stories say. Their flowers never faded, and their leaves never withered. However, they were not invulnerable. Early humanoids hunted amaranth dragons to test the truth of their immortality, trying various cruel methods to kill the dragons. When these hunters inevitably failed, they gave up and abandoned the dragons to a slow recovery.

One such hunter, Juan, felt remorse for their cruelty and took in an amaranth dragon they had grievously injured. They renounced hunting, nursed the dragon back to health, and gained its trust. Juan and the dragon became close companions, with the amaranth dragon acting as a scout and tracker for the former hunter.

Juan and the dragon adventured together for many years until Juan was too weak and frail to continue. The amaranth dragon realized that its friend was dying and that it would outlive every other humanoid friend it made. Grief-stricken, the amaranth dragon assembled its kin in a great congregation, the likes of which have never been seen again. Juan's dragon explained the joy of a deep connection and the pain of losing Juan. After hearing out the lamenting dragon, the dragons came to a consensus. They would ask the gods for two things—an end to their immortality and a lasting friendship between amaranth dragons and humanoids.
The god of compassion heard the dragons' prayers and granted their wish: the amaranth dragons would be companions to humanoids and would no longer outlive their friends.
Juan's amaranth dragon died peacefully. Since then, amaranth dragons have lived out the rest of their now-mortal lives as friends to humanoids.

entries.name: Physiology
entries: Amaranth dragons can grow up to six feet in length, not including their tails, which can be as long as their bodies. Today, they live for around 80 years, with the oldest recorded amaranth dragon living to the age of 83. Their flowers bloom most commonly in red, but shades of lighter pink and reddish purples are also possible. Despite their bright red flowers, amaranth dragons have excellent camouflage and hide in plain sight. They can stay very still, blending in with their environment. Wanderers often believe that the dragons' flowery tails are simply amaranth plants growing in the wild. Amaranth dragons have strong, root-like claws that allow them to secure themselves to trees. They boast excellent vision, even at night.
